scenarioStory.history: Restrained driver involved in a moderate-speed T-bone collision approximately 20 minutes ago; airbag deployed. Since the crash, patient reports constant, severe lower abdominal pain and has noted vaginal bleeding soaking through her clothing. Denies loss of consciousness. Reports decreased fetal movement over the last several minutes.
scenarioStory.course: Initial Contact: Crew arrives to find a 33-year-old, 32-weeks-pregnant female still in the driver's seat, alert and in visible distress with abdominal pain and vaginal bleeding. She is currently supine/semi-reclined in the seat. → Left lateral positioning and IV fluids started: Crew completes a MARCH primary survey, positions the patient in the left lateral recumbent position to relieve aortocaval compression, establishes large-bore IV access, and begins rapid crystalloid resuscitation. → Perfusion improves, transport initiated: Vital signs trend toward normal with fluid resuscitation and left lateral positioning. Crew reassesses serially and transports emergently to the closest appropriate obstetric/trauma-capable facility with advance notification.

patientInformation.patientCondition: Vaginal bleeding and abdominal pain after motor vehicle collision, 32 weeks pregnant

scenarioEvents.name: Initial Contact
scenarioEvents.description: Crew arrives to find a 33-year-old, 32-weeks-pregnant female still in the driver's seat, alert and in visible distress with abdominal pain and vaginal bleeding. She is currently supine/semi-reclined in the seat.

scenarioEvents.name: Left lateral positioning and IV fluids started
scenarioEvents.description: Crew completes a MARCH primary survey, positions the patient in the left lateral recumbent position to relieve aortocaval compression, establishes large-bore IV access, and begins rapid crystalloid resuscitation.
relatedChecklist: Perform MARCH primary survey to rule out other life threats before focusing on OB findings
Position patient left lateral recumbent given third-trimester shock
Establish large-bore IV; begin crystalloid resuscitation, 1-2 L wide open
Save all passed vaginal tissue/pads for receiving team assessment

scenarioEvents.name: Perfusion improves, transport initiated
scenarioEvents.description: Vital signs trend toward normal with fluid resuscitation and left lateral positioning. Crew reassesses serially and transports emergently to the closest appropriate obstetric/trauma-capable facility with advance notification.
relatedChecklist: Reassess vital signs and response to fluid resuscitation serially en route
Transport emergently to closest appropriate facility; notify en route

scenarioEvents.name: Left lateral positioning not maintained
scenarioEvents.description: The patient is packaged and transported supine. Without left lateral tilt, the gravid uterus compresses the inferior vena cava, causing a sudden drop in venous return and worsening hypotension despite ongoing fluid resuscitation.
relatedChecklist: Recognize supine hypotension; reposition left lateral or manually displace uterus left
